subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Inequality of Polluted Air
description: Learn The Inequality of Polluted Air in one minute.

hook.text: 97% of cities in low-income countries exceed WHO air quality guidelines. In rich countries, 49%.

buildup.text: Poorer neighborhoods sit closer to highways, factories, and power plants.

discovery.text: In the US, Black and Hispanic communities breathe 50% more NO₂ than white communities.

twist.text: The people who contribute least to pollution often suffer the most from it.

climax.text: Environmental justice movements demand that clean air is a right, not a privilege.

punchline.text: Your zip code predicts your air quality better than your lifestyle.

quiz.question: Which communities tend to experience the worst air quality?

details.summary: Air pollution exposure is deeply unequal. Low-income communities and racial minorities are disproportionately located near highways, industrial facilities, and waste sites, bearing a far greater pollution burden than wealthier populations.
details.whyItMatters: Environmental injustice means the people least responsible for pollution suffer the most. Recognizing this inequity is essential for designing fair clean-air policies.
takeaways: Polluting facilities are disproportionately sited near minority communities
Low-income populations have less access to healthcare for pollution-related illness
Environmental justice movements push for equitable pollution reduction

faq.question: Why are polluting facilities more common in low-income areas?
faq.answer: Historically cheap land, less political resistance, and discriminatory zoning practices like redlining concentrated industrial facilities and highways near communities of color and low-income neighborhoods.

faq.question: What is the environmental justice movement?
faq.answer: It is a social movement demanding that no community bear a disproportionate share of environmental harm. It advocates for equal enforcement of environmental laws and meaningful participation in decisions affecting community health.
